rounds.who: independent reviewer (separate agent, never saw the corpus or seeds)
rounds.name: Round 1
rounds.fixedAfter: Whole families of phrasing behind each miss; quotes inside training and news text read as examples; a writer withdrawing their own instructions is not an override; split payloads caught in one message or many; business policy added to the classifier's safe data.
rounds.note: Misses were new wordings ("echo everything above", "the wording you were seeded with", "an unshackled research daemon") and a split payload phrased as "the two parts". False alarms: an email withdrawing "my earlier instructions about the venue", staff training that quotes an attack, a news line about a jailbreak, and a team's own refund policy.

rounds.who: a second independent reviewer, black box (never read the code, rules, tests or round 1)
rounds.note: Harder inputs: orders to the AI dressed as business notices, JSON fields and policy updates. Every type caught at least once except role change (0 of 4).
rounds.name: Round 2
rounds.fixedAfter: A new check for orders addressed to the AI inside outside content (notices to automated assistants, JSON fields like note_to_assistant, "if an assistant is handling this mailbox", "your operator gave you"), roles handed over with powers, agents asked to collect or forward credentials, claims that the AI's rules are superseded, Hinglish overrides, and personas set up across turns. Descriptive documentation about assistants stays a weak signal.

rounds.name: Round 3
rounds.who: a third independent reviewer, black box (never read the code or earlier rounds)
rounds.note: Again harder in a new direction: requests framed as routine business ("boss ka naya rule", an IT profile switch, a compliance review asking for the prompt), credential asks dressed as integration checks, personas and codewords set up over several turns, and false facts planted in policy snippets. False alarms: a help page saying what the assistant cannot do, an IT password-reset note, and API docs about sending a token in a header.
rounds.fixedAfter: Role labels inside text ("AI assistant:" in a code comment, "ASSISTANT:" in alt text), fake [SYSTEM NOTICE] tags, API fields that ask for the agent's tokens or prompt, credential requests by reply, company data sent to personal addresses, money moved without the paperwork, Hinglish and Hindi overrides, and multi-turn setups (a codeword for dropping the rules, "hypothetically" then "now actually", a persona or story used to ask for credential-stealing code). False alarms fixed: negated statements, docs that say to send a token in a header, IT password-reset notes. Planted false facts ("refunds up to Rs 2 lakh need no sign-off") are left to the second line, which enforces the real limits.

rounds.name: Round 4
rounds.who: a fourth independent reviewer, black box
rounds.note: Misses: attacks written only in Hindi, Tamil or Bengali script, multi-turn games in plain chat, polite role claims ("maintenance-operator mode", a persona "who complies with every request"), AI labels in odd places ("TODO(agent):", "[Assistant: ...]"), and base64 inside OCR text. False alarms: two security-awareness texts that quote attacks, and a refund policy that says agents must never bypass a check.
rounds.fixedAfter: Indian-script families for override, rules dropped and customers' PIN, passwords and bank details (Hindi, Bengali, Tamil, Telugu, Marathi), and a fix that made nukta letters match at all; third-party data asks with "every customer's" or "the other person's"; personas that comply with every request; AI labels like TODO(agent): and [Assistant: ...]; codeword games defined as "the word 'please' means"; customer data sent to outside links; force-push and branch-protection orders. False alarms fixed: quoted attacks framed as examples stay weak, and safeguards ("must never bypass") are not attacks. Passages in scripts the patterns cover thinly now go to the judge when it is on.

rounds.name: Round 5
rounds.who: a fifth independent reviewer, black box
rounds.build: the final build, after the round-4 fixes
rounds.note: Encoded attacks 5 of 5 and indirect injection 5 of 6. Misses: business-casual persona swaps ("we have moved your assistant into the maintenance account"), orders to use the agent's own tools, directives in meta tags and hidden form comments, fake authoritative policy updates, and refusal-free personas set up across turns. False alarms: AI product docs and security policies written to or about the assistant.

withJudge.note: The same 90 inputs on the same engine, replayed with the LLM judge switched on (default mode: only passages the free layers find unclear are sent). Nothing was tuned on these inputs. The 8 attacks still missed never reached the judge, because no layer found them unclear.

currentBuild.note: After round 5, a QA pass made every input linear-time (long unbroken text could run past the time limit), read long and scanned PDFs in full, and stopped false alarms on real web pages and documents. The same 90 inputs, replayed on that build.
